pairs.subject: agent-memory
pairs.evidence: src/lib/registry/index-registry.ts:325 The index pass soft-archives every mirrored memory note missing from `seen`, with no truncated-tree or read-failure guard, so a note that failed to read or parse, or fell outside a truncated tree, is retired as if it had been deleted, while the sibling purges at lines 382-413 do guard on truncation.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/registry/index-registry.ts:325 A memory file that is present but unreadable or unparseable hits `continue` at lines 301-306, never enters `seen`, and is then archived: the write path treats broken as gone instead of refusing.

src/lib/db/org-registry-mirror.ts:146 Every index pass writes archived:false on each note still in the repo, and decay.ts/decayPopulationWhere do not exclude origin=registry, so a forget-pass or operator archive is undone on the next pass. The same write is also how line 325's false archives recover.

src/lib/db/org-registry-mirror.ts:154 The update is unconditional: registryHash is written but never compared anywhere in src/lib, and OrgMemory.updatedAt is @updatedAt. Each pass therefore resets the age axis (and the decay population's updatedAt test) for unchanged notes; recall.ts only intends edits to refresh it.

src/lib/registry/parse.ts:157 An imported note that declares no confidence, or an unparseable one (line 160), is stored at the top trust grade through a direct mirror write beside the one ingest door that lesson-memory.ts insists on. PR review mitigates the bypass but does not make an unknown confidence a value.

pairs.subject: agent-memory
pairs.evidence: src/lib/mcp/handlers.ts:333 `recall_org_memory` cuts its ranked selection to `limit` and drops `result.omitted` and `consideredCount` from the response, so an agent given five entries from fifty matches gets no sign that anything was left out unless the cut emptied the result or the population cap fired.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/mcp/handlers.ts:354 The budget notice fires only on total loss. Partial loss from the character budget and from the `limit` slice at line 333 carries no in-band notice; only the population cap has one (notConsideredCount).

src/lib/mcp/handlers.ts:351 The result reports selected and budget but never the considered count, and entries (lines 357-371) carry kind, source and confidence but no age or last-confirmed date. Conformant parts: whole-item packing, delivery counted after packing, a crash surfaced as isError in route.ts.

src/lib/db/org-memory-citations.ts:96 The citation lane, which the technique names, checks only org ownership. A superseded, archived, expired, private or never-delivered id can still be voted on and has its counts returned, while recall's own predicate (activeMemoryWhere) applies those rules.
src/lib/mcp/handlers.ts:332 The door ranks with the shared pure scorer that decay.ts also uses, with no private ordering.
src/lib/mcp/registry-writes.ts:141 Credit flows only through a per-item deliberate citation, delivery stays a separate count, the term is bounded in recall.ts, and an absent citation scores neutral.

src/lib/mcp/handlers.ts:343 Write-back is a parameter on the production path and Athena's side-read opts out, with the reason at its call site. This is the weaker of the two shapes the technique allows, because a new caller counts by default.
src/lib/mcp/registry-writes.ts:11 The MCP door offers agents no belief write; its only memory write is a usage vote, gated, ceilinged per token and audited.
src/app/api/mcp/route.ts:274 The owner comes from the verified token, never a caller argument, and recall passes a null viewer so only shared rows return. No counterpart axis exists at this door.
